questions.stem: Why can carbon be used to extract metals like iron and zinc from their oxides?

options.text: Because carbon is more reactive than these metals and can take their oxygen away
Because carbon has a very low melting point

questions.explanation: Carbon is placed between aluminium and zinc in the reactivity series. It is more reactive than metals below it (such as zinc, iron, lead, copper), so it can remove oxygen from their oxides in a displacement-type reaction.

questions.stem: What is the balanced equation for the reduction of iron(III) oxide with carbon?
questions.explanation: 2Fe₂O₃ + 3C → 4Fe + 3CO₂ is the balanced equation. The carbon removes the oxygen from the iron oxide, reducing it to iron metal. The carbon is oxidised to carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: In the blast furnace, what is the actual reducing agent that reduces iron ore?
questions.explanation: In the blast furnace, coke (carbon) first reacts with oxygen to form carbon dioxide, which then reacts with more coke to form carbon monoxide. It is the carbon monoxide that is the main reducing agent: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.

questions.stem: In the reaction ZnO + C → Zn + CO, which substance is oxidised and which is reduced?

options.text: Carbon is reduced; zinc oxide is oxidised
Carbon is oxidised; zinc oxide is reduced

questions.explanation: Carbon is oxidised because it gains oxygen (C → CO). Zinc oxide is reduced because it loses oxygen (ZnO → Zn). This is a redox reaction where carbon acts as the reducing agent.

questions.stem: Which metal CANNOT be extracted by reduction with carbon?
questions.explanation: Aluminium cannot be extracted by reduction with carbon because aluminium is more reactive than carbon. Only metals below carbon in the reactivity series can be reduced by carbon. Aluminium must be extracted by electrolysis.

questions.stem: What role does limestone (CaCO₃) play in the blast furnace?

options.text: It is the fuel that heats the furnace
It acts as the reducing agent
It removes impurities (like sand) from the iron ore by forming slag
It prevents the iron from rusting

questions.explanation: Limestone decomposes in the furnace to form calcium oxide (CaO), which reacts with sandy impurities (silicon dioxide) to form calcium silicate (slag). This removes impurities from the iron. The coke is the fuel and the source of the reducing agent.

questions.stem: What are the three raw materials added to the blast furnace to extract iron?

options.text: Iron ore, carbon dioxide, and water

questions.explanation: The three raw materials are iron ore (contains iron oxide), coke (a form of carbon, acts as fuel and provides the reducing agent), and limestone (removes impurities). Hot air is also blasted in to react with the coke.
